The Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey, 2025 to 2026
Themes

The Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey is the shorter version of the full surveys the country has run every five years since 1989. It carries a shorter questionnaire, focusing on asking women aged 15 to 49 about pregnancy and childbirth, their children's health and feeding, family planning, and the conditions of the households they live in. Data was collected from November 2025 to February 2026 in a sample powered at the county level.

26,380 households visited
21,231 women age 15 to 49 interviewed
47 counties, all of them

    Or start from the figures below and the 15 chapters underneath them.

    Themes
    Kenya at a glance

    Health outcomes

    What the survey counted happening, rather than what was provided.

    Health service coverage

    What reached the women and children who needed it. A service is not a result.

    Nutrition

    No child in this survey was weighed or measured, so it produces no stunting, wasting or underweight figure. The report's own list of Sustainable Development Goal indicators shows the same gap, carrying dietary diversity alone under zero hunger. The most recent measured figures are the 2022 survey's.

    Fertility and family formation

    When childbearing starts and how much of it there is.

    Living conditions

    What the household has, which is where most of the difference between counties sits.

    Developed by the Centre for Epidemiological Modelling and Analysis at the University of Nairobi, from the tables published by the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics.

    The Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey 2025/26 was carried out by the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics with the Ministry of Health and technical assistance from The DHS Program at ICF. Fieldwork ran from November 2025 to February 2026 and interviewed 21,231 women age 15 to 49 in 1,000 clusters across all 47 counties. Every figure on this site is taken from a published table of that survey and shown as published, marks and all.

    Where the opening page says what a figure has moved from, the earlier figure is named. Most come from the 2014 and 2022 Kenya Demographic and Health Surveys. The maternal mortality ratio is the exception, because the 2022 survey carried no maternal mortality module, so it is shown against the 2019 census and the 2014 survey. County boundaries follow the 47 counties of the 2010 Constitution.
